name: Hotel Plaza Athenee Paris
positioning: Hotel Plaza Athenee on avenue Montaigne in Paris, within walking distance of the Eiffel Tower and the Champs-Elysees, with an Art Deco brasserie, a Dior spa and a gilded fine-dining room
best_for: Travelers who want a walkable Paris base near the Eiffel Tower and the Champs-Elysees
Fashion lovers who want to stay on avenue Montaigne
Food lovers interested in heritage French cuisine and pastry

facts.text: The hotel is at 25 avenue Montaigne, within walking distance of the Eiffel Tower and the Champs-Elysees.
Avenue Montaigne has a view of the Eiffel Tower at one end and the Champs-Elysees at the other.
Avenue Montaigne is home to high-fashion flagships, including number 30, the building where Dior was founded in 1946.
Le Relais Plaza has original Diane Chasseresse frescoes, a Lalique chandelier and engraved zodiac stained glass.
At La Grande Table du Plaza Athenee, the chefs give a fresh take on ancient French recipes, some up to 250 years old.
Le Cabinet des Conspirateurs is a private dining room set within the kitchen, behind glass doors.
Executive pastry chef Angelo Musa won the World Pastry Chef award and was named Meilleur Ouvrier de France in 2007.
Afternoon tea is served daily at La Galerie.
La Galerie passes the day to the sound of harps.
Two bakers start the bread at 3am to bring guests fresh rolls every morning.
The Dior Light Suite is a light therapy room with circadian-supportive lighting and treatments to help rebalance the sleep cycle.
Le Bar has a display of Dom Perignon champagnes designed by Nicolas Francart.

highlights.text: Le Relais Plaza is one of the city's last remaining Art Deco dining rooms, with a 1930s spirit.
La Grande Table centres on a Royal Table of antique Breccia pink marble, in a room by designer Remi Tessier with 20,000 gold leaves and a gilded ceiling.
Le Bar was redesigned in 2014 by Patrick Jouin and Sanjit Manku, with a deep blue fabric ceiling over a transparent bar made from a single block of resin.
The hotel has its own fruit chef.
The hotel runs its spa in partnership with Dior.

considerations.text: At La Grande Table, elegant attire is requested: a jacket is recommended for men, and caps, shorts and sportswear are not permitted.
Le Bar does not admit unaccompanied children.
WhataHotel notes ultra-luxury pricing and a formal atmosphere that may feel intimidating to casual travelers.
